page.layout: One printed page, single column of running text, with the running head at top centre-left and the page number at top right. Nothing printed in the margins. The left strip of the scan is the edge of the facing page and is not transcribed.

main_text.p: vertat corda patrum ad filios, & infideles instrue-at in sapientia justorum p pulum paratum Do-mino. Nempe ut sint populus paratus Domino. Est enim τὸ λαὸν κατεσκευασμένον appositivum τῷ, ἀπειθεῖς. Ut convertat corda patrum ad filios, vel ut vertit Pagninus Malach. 4. 5. cor patrum super filios & cor filiorum super patres eorum, intelligendum reor, usque ad filios &c. ut τὸ בער & τὸ ὅτι quandoque significant in veteri, i e. ut plane Vatablus, ut convertat patres unà cum filiis. Occurrit omninò eadem di-stionis formula Judith. 9. 10. πάταξον δοῦλον ἐν χείλεσιν ἀπάτης μου ἐπ' ἀρχοντα ἡ ἀρχοντα ὅτι διεφθαρται αὐτος. Percute servum ex labiis deceptionis meæ super principem & principem super ministrum ejus, ut est in versione Latina, i. e. ut in Malachia, usque ad principem & principem usque ad ministrum ejus, vel ut vertimus anglicè magis plane, Smite by the reeeit of my lips the servant with the Prince and the Prince with the servant. Ut etiam vertit Junius, Percute servum labiis fraudulentis meis cum Domino & Dominum cum servo ipsius. Officium enim erat præcursoris, qui parabat vias Domini, resipiscentiam prædicare omnibus hominibus à patribus ad filios & a filiis ad patres, ut pareatiores fierent ad recipiendum, quod appropinquabat, regnum Dei. τὸ ἐν φρονήσει δικαίων ἑτοιμάσας, & τὸ δοῦναι γνῶσιν σωτηρίας &c. v. 77. unum idemque signifi-cant, est enim tantùm verborum periphrasis, in utrisque verò locis unus idemque sensus.
V. 54, 55. Ἀντελάβετο Ἰσραὴλ παιδὸς αὐτοῦ μνησθῆναι ἐλέους ( καθὼς ἐλάλησε πρὸς τοὺς πατέρας ἡμῶν ) τῷ Ἀβραὰμ καὶ τῷ σπέρματι αὐτοῦ εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα. Et sublevavit filium suum

page.notes: The first line's opening word is partly cut off at the left edge of the column; read as "vertat" with the probable letters of "convertat" missing, so a [?] applies. The Hebrew letters in the Malachi/Hebrew reference (ut τὸ ...) are only approximately legible and should be checked against the scan. The Greek passages are transcribed from a fairly degraded print and may contain small errors in accents and letters. "Domino" in the second paragraph and "Latina" are as far as I can make out. The marginal left strip is the neighbouring page and is omitted.
